newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mayne sees improved year performance.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mayne sees improved year performance.

text.p: Transport and health care group Mayne Nickless Ltd said on Thursday that it was on track for a better result for the full year to June 30, 1997.
"We believe we are on track for a much improved performance for the full 1997 year," Chief Financial Officer Shane Tanner told a news conference.
Mayne reported a fall in net profit to A$43.14 million for the six months to December 31, but operating profit rose 8.1 percent to A$88.145 million.
There was an A$21.42 million abnormal loss.
"Despite the fact that EBIT (earnings before interest and tax) was off, we are fairly encouraged by the underlying business trend," Tanner said.
EBIT fell 0.7 percent to A$101.4 million in the first half.
Tanner said the company was working to reduce its overheads.
"On a go-forward basis, I would expect our unallocated costs to revert in the second half back to where they were last year," he said.
